function: Precoder design and common-rate allocation for 1-layer RSMA in downlink near-field ELAA under imperfect CSIT and SIC, maximizing the geometric mean of ergodic user rates (pp. 7-8)
system: Downlink FDD, BS with UPA of M=19x19 elements serving K=20 single-antenna users, near-field, 3.5 GHz, half-wavelength spacing, no RIS (pp. 3, 9, 10)
method: GruCN: GRU module plus CNN module and fully connected generation layers; unsupervised training with a geometric-mean-rate loss over Y=10 CSIT samples, Adam, 1000 iterations (pp. 7-9)
data_channel: Simulated near-field mixed LoS/NLoS non-stationary ELAA channel following [59]: Rician/Rayleigh fading, log-normal shadowing, Gaussian CSIT error; 70%/30% train/test split (pp. 4, 9)
test_conditions: Same simulated distribution for training and testing (70%/30% split); sweeps of SNR, antennas, users, CSIT quality and SIC factor; no cross-setting test stated (pp. 9-12)
baselines: Non-learned: ZF precoding with SDMA and RSMA (RSMA-ZF, SDMA-ZF); learned: MLP with five FC layers, CNN with three CNN layers, under SDMA and RSMA (p. 9)
metrics: GMER, minimum ergodic user rate and ergodic sum rate versus SNR, antennas, users, CSIT quality and SIC error; CPU processing time; training loss (pp. 10-13)
complexity: Big-O order for GruCN versus O((KMY)^3.5 log(1/eps)) for iterative optimization (p. 9); CPU time about 0.001 s versus over 0.2 s for ZF (p. 12)
openness: none; no code or data release, link or DOI stated
q1_support: p. 4: "non-stationary channel model according to [59]" (Bernoulli LoS/NLoS, Rician and Rayleigh fading, log-normal shadowing); p. 9: "channel model described in Section II" generates the samples. No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "is carefully divided into training and testing sets following" a 70%:30% ratio of the same simulated data; M, N, delta and rho are swept (pp. 10-12), but the paper never says that a model trained for one setting is tested on another.
q3_support: p. 9: "(1) the conventional ZF precoding" is the non-learned baseline; "(2) Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) [74] with five FC" layers and a CNN are the learned baselines; p. 10: "our proposed GruCN model outperforms conventional MLP" and CNN in GMER (Fig. 4a).
q4_support: p. 9: "the total complexity of the GruCN is" O((zeta^2 L_C + 2 L_G) Y iota^2), against O((KMY)^3.5 log(1/eps)) for iterative optimization; p. 12: "approximately 0.001 seconds for precoder design" (Fig. 9, CPU time).
q5_support: p. 9: "channel model described in Section II" generates its own samples; no code or data link or DOI is given, and no public dataset or measured data is used.
notes: Area 3 chosen: the learned GruCN designs the BS precoder and the common-rate allocation (p. 7). q1 is 0 because the channel follows the academic non-stationary ELAA model of [59] (Liu, Ma and Tafazolli), not a standardized model; the reviewer may confirm. q2 is 0: one 70/30 split and no stated cross-setting test, and the network input and output sizes depend on M and K. RIS appears only in related work (p. 1), not in the system.
